samples.summary: GitHub sign-in can silently switch to a different email address, splitting an existing account
samples.evidence: `verifiedEmail()` picks `verified.find(isFlagSet(primary)) ?? verified[0]` — i.e. when the primary address is *unverified* it falls back to some other verified address. The email is the sole identity `UserService.findOrCreateUser` matches on (user.service.ts:129-133), so an existing user whose row was created under their (unverified) primary address will, on their next login, arrive under a different address, miss the existing row, and be created as a brand-new user with a brand-new workspace (createUserWithWorkspace). Their documents, workspaces, API keys and memberships stay attached to the old row and become unreachable. Worse, the old row is never stamped with `emailVerifiedAt`, so a later Google sign-in on that address is permanently refused with `email_conflict` (user.service.ts:135-138) — the remedy the error text prescribes ("sign in with GitHub once") can never succeed for that user. Additionally, `/user/emails` has no documented ordering, so `verified[0]` is not stable between logins when several non-primary verified addresses exist.

samples.summary: Every GitHub login is refused when passport cannot fetch /user/emails (flags absent), e.g. GitHub Enterprise without GITHUB_USER_EMAIL_URL
samples.evidence: `verifiedEmail()` requires an explicit truthy `verified` flag on an entry. `passport-github2` only populates flag-carrying entries when the `/user/emails` request succeeds; when that request errors (missing scope on an existing token, GHE deployment whose `GITHUB_USER_EMAIL_URL` is unset so the call hits api.github.com with a GHE token — the exact case the comment at github.strategy.ts:77-79 documents, rate limiting, transient 5xx) the strategy falls back to `Profile.parse(json)`, whose `emails` entry is `[{ value: json.email }]` with no `verified` flag. `verifiedEmail` then returns undefined and *every* login on that deployment is refused with `unverified_email` — a total auth outage, indistinguishable from a genuinely unverified account. A transient email-endpoint failure should not be reported as 'your email is unverified' / deny the login outright.

samples.summary: A concurrent first sign-in (P2002 on User.email) escapes the callback's /login?error= contract as a 500
samples.evidence: `if (!isSlugConflict(error) || attempt >= SLUG_ATTEMPTS) throw error;` deliberately rethrows a duplicate-email P2002 (comment at lines 196-198 acknowledges it means a concurrent sign-in already created the user). That exception propagates out of `resolveOAuthUser` (auth.controller.ts:271-276 only catches `EmailProviderConflictError`) and out of the callback, so the browser lands on backend JSON instead of the login page, and a CLI login gets nothing at its loopback listener and blocks for the full five-minute timeout — exactly the failure mode the rest of this change exists to avoid. Retrying the `findUnique` once on a duplicate-email conflict would make it a successful login instead.

samples.summary: Cross-provider conflict can be permanent for users whose original provider can no longer prove the address
samples.evidence: `throw new EmailProviderConflictError(user.authProvider)` on any `emailVerifiedAt === null` row. The only way to clear it is a same-provider sign-in (lines 139-144), but that sign-in now itself requires a verified address at the provider (github.strategy.ts:144). A legacy GitHub row created from an address that is not verified today therefore cannot be stamped at all: the GitHub login either refuses (`unverified_email`) or, per the fallback above, arrives under a different address and creates a second account. The user is left permanently unable to use the other provider and with no in-product remedy, while the error message tells them to do something that cannot work.

samples.summary: GET /auth/providers reports github: true unconditionally, even when GitHub OAuth is not configured
samples.evidence: `return { github: true, google: googleAuthConfigured() };` — unlike Google, GitHub's configuration is never checked. On a deployment with `GOOGLE_*` set but `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`/`GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` unset (now a possible configuration, since Google is a full alternative login), the login page still renders the GitHub button and clicking it fails inside passport rather than being hidden like the Google one. The endpoint's stated purpose is 'which sign-in buttons the login page should offer'.

samples.summary: Google callback leaves the OAuth state cookie behind when the state token is not web-shaped
samples.evidence: The `||` chain short-circuits: when `typeof stateToken !== 'string'` or `!isWebOAuthState(stateToken)`, `consumeWebOAuthState` (the only thing that calls `res.clearCookie` for the state cookie) never runs, so the ten-minute state cookie survives a refused callback. Harmless in practice (it is single-use against a hash it cannot match) but it contradicts the stated invariant in web-oauth-login.ts:60-61 that 'the cookie is cleared whether or not it matches, so a failed login leaves nothing behind'.

samples.summary: Non-null assertions on profile fields can turn a missing username into a TypeError before Prisma validates
samples.evidence: `auth.controller.ts:267-268` passes `profile.username!` / `profile.email!` although `OAuthProfile` declares both optional, and `createUserWithWorkspace` then calls `workspaceSlugBase(data.username)` which does `username.toLowerCase()` (user.service.ts:38). A GitHub profile without `username` (the typings mark it optional) therefore crashes with `Cannot read properties of undefined` inside the service rather than failing with a routed refusal or a Prisma validation error. Low reach, but the assertions are load-bearing and unchecked.

finding.summary: GitHub sign-in can silently switch to a different email address, splitting an existing account
finding.evidence: `verifiedEmail()` picks `verified.find(isFlagSet(primary)) ?? verified[0]` — i.e. when the primary address is *unverified* it falls back to some other verified address. The email is the sole identity `UserService.findOrCreateUser` matches on (user.service.ts:129-133), so an existing user whose row was created under their (unverified) primary address will, on their next login, arrive under a different address, miss the existing row, and be created as a brand-new user with a brand-new workspace (createUserWithWorkspace). Their documents, workspaces, API keys and memberships stay attached to the old row and become unreachable. Worse, the old row is never stamped with `emailVerifiedAt`, so a later Google sign-in on that address is permanently refused with `email_conflict` (user.service.ts:135-138) — the remedy the error text prescribes ("sign in with GitHub once") can never succeed for that user. Additionally, `/user/emails` has no documented ordering, so `verified[0]` is not stable between logins when several non-primary verified addresses exist.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is present verbatim: github.strategy.ts:63 selects `verified.find((e) => isFlagSet(e.primary)) ?? verified[0]`, so an unverified primary silently shifts the sign-in address to another verified address whose index depends on GitHub's undocumented /user/emails ordering. user.service.ts:128-133 matches identity on email alone and user.service.ts:147 falls through to createUserWithWorkspace, which creates a new user plus a new workspace and owner membership (lines 176-193). I grepped all of packages/backend/src for any githubId-based lookup and found none (githubId is only emitted by the strategy at github.strategy.ts:129,150, never used as a reconciliation key), so no guard elsewhere makes the split unreachable. The path does not even require pre-existing legacy rows: sign in once while the primary is unverified (row under fallback address B), then verify the primary on GitHub, and the next login resolves to the primary, misses the B row, and creates a second account while the first one's documents/workspaces stay orphaned. The email_conflict corollary also reproduces (user.service.ts:135-138 into auth.controller.ts:272-273), though the reviewer overstates it as permanent: verifying the address on GitHub does unblock it via the stamp at lines 141-144. That detail does not undermine the core account-splitting defect, which is in-lane (broken invariant, user data made unreachable) and blocking at major.

finding.summary: Every GitHub login is refused when passport cannot fetch /user/emails (flags absent), e.g. GitHub Enterprise without GITHUB_USER_EMAIL_URL
finding.evidence: `verifiedEmail()` requires an explicit truthy `verified` flag on an entry. `passport-github2` only populates flag-carrying entries when the `/user/emails` request succeeds; when that request errors (missing scope on an existing token, GHE deployment whose `GITHUB_USER_EMAIL_URL` is unset so the call hits api.github.com with a GHE token — the exact case the comment at github.strategy.ts:77-79 documents, rate limiting, transient 5xx) the strategy falls back to `Profile.parse(json)`, whose `emails` entry is `[{ value: json.email }]` with no `verified` flag. `verifiedEmail` then returns undefined and *every* login on that deployment is refused with `unverified_email` — a total auth outage, indistinguishable from a genuinely unverified account. A transient email-endpoint failure should not be reported as 'your email is unverified' / deny the login outright.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `verifiedEmail()` (github.strategy.ts:58-65) keeps only entries whose `verified` flag is explicitly true per `isFlagSet` (:29-31), so an entry shaped `{ value: 'x' }` with no `verified` key yields undefined, and `validate()` (:144-146) then refuses with `unverified_email`. The repo's own spec case 'nothing verified' (github.strategy.spec.ts:181) asserts that this exact flagless shape is refused — which is the shape produced when passport-github2 falls back after a failed /user/emails fetch. `GITHUB_USER_EMAIL_URL` is optional-by-spread (:92) and the comment at :77-79 documents that a GHE deployment without it sends a GHE token to api.github.com and fails, and the endpoint specs (spec.ts:34-40) confirm the github.com default is used when the var is unset. I found no guard anywhere that requires the var, distinguishes an errored email fetch from a genuinely unverified account, or otherwise makes the path unreachable; the transient cases (rate limit, 5xx, token lacking the scope) are not config-dependent at all. This is error handling that reports an infrastructure failure as an authorization verdict and denies the request on a reachable path — correctness lane. I could not inspect passport-github2's source (node_modules absent), which is residual uncertainty that argues for keeping the finding rather than dropping it. No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Google sign-up crashes (500) and leaves an orphaned user row when the display-name-derived workspace slug collides
finding.evidence: `AuthController.googleAuthCallback` (auth.controller.ts:280) calls `findOrCreateUser({ username: googleUser.username, ... })` where `username` is now `profile.displayName` (google.strategy.ts:75), which is NOT unique and NOT restricted to ASCII. `findOrCreateUser` derives the workspace slug naively: `newUser.username.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,'-').replace(/^-+|-+$/g,'') + '-s-workspace'` (user.service.ts:54-58) and `Workspace.slug` is `@unique` (schema.prisma:168). So (a) any non-Latin display name (e.g. '홍길동', '李') reduces to the empty base and yields the single slug `-s-workspace`, and (b) two Google accounts named 'John Smith', or the email-local-part fallback for ada@a.com and ada@b.com, yield identical slugs. The second such signup: `prisma.user.create` succeeds, then `prisma.workspace.create` throws P2002 — there is no transaction and no catch anywhere up to the controller — so the request 500s and the user row survives with no workspace, permanently broken (the retry now takes the existing-user branch and never creates a workspace). This was previously unreachable because GitHub `username` is a globally-unique ASCII login. The codebase already knows this hazard: `WorkspaceService.generateUniqueSlug` (workspace.service.ts:22, 277-281) dedupes and falls back to a neutral base for exactly the empty-slug case; `findOrCreateUser` does not use it.

verdict.reason: The finding describes user.service.ts as deriving the workspace slug naively (username -> slug + '-s-workspace') with no transaction and no P2002 handling, leaving an orphaned user row. The file does not contain that code. `workspaceSlugBase` (user.service.ts:37-43) returns the neutral base 'workspace' when the name reduces to empty, so the '-s-workspace' / non-ASCII case is handled; `freeSlug` (user.service.ts:46-56) looks the base up and appends a random hex suffix when taken, so two identical display names ('John Smith') or two email-local-part fallbacks get distinct slugs; and `createUserWithWorkspace` (user.service.ts:176-194) performs user.create, workspace.create and workspaceMember.create inside `this.prisma.$transaction`, so a workspace failure rolls the user row back — no orphan can survive. `isSlugConflict` (user.service.ts:58-68) plus the retry loop (user.service.ts:174, 195-200, SLUG_ATTEMPTS at line 26) covers the check-then-insert race. The lines the reviewer cites (54-58) are the body of `freeSlug`, not a naive concatenation. The call path is real (auth.controller.ts:265 with username from google.strategy.ts:75-77), but the crash/orphan outcome cannot occur against this code, and user.service.spec.ts:130-144, 148-157 and 159-170 assert exactly the three claimed scenarios behave correctly.
